text.p: An explosive device went off on Monday in the compound of the headquarters of the Yugoslav United Left (JUL) party led by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's wife Mirjana Markovic, a party source told Reuters.
"An explosive device exploded half an hour ago between two buildings at JUL headquarters, causing damage but no injuries. A communique will issued in minutes," the JUL source said.
The party later issued a terse statement confirming the explosion.
"An explosive device was thrown at the headquarters of the Yugoslav left in Belgrade. Material damage was inflicted on the facilities, there were no casualties," the statement said.
The police had no immediate statement.
A Reuters photographer who arrived on the scene saw several police cars and another journalist reported damage to the building's facade and some windows shattered.
Leaders of the Zajedno (Together) pro-democracy movement denied involvement in the bombing and one suggested it had been staged.
"The disgraceful regime is resorting to its last desperate attempts to remain in power by staging some sort of bombing of JUL," Vuk Draskovic, a Zajedno leader, said.

The attack was bound to raise tensions since JUL has insisted on a police crackdown on supporters of the opposition who have been protesting in Belgrade and other towns in Serbia demanding that Milosevic restore opposition election gains.

The incident coincided with what witnesses and police officers said was the biggest protest demonstration in Belgrade to date as several hundred thousand Zajedno supporters thronged Belgrade's central square for Orthodox Christmas festivities.
